statement.excerpt: Agency plus LLMs have already led multiple “vibe coders” to lose databases, with new reports coming in every day or two, stemming simply from the unreliability inherent in LLMs (that Gary has so often harped on).

our_interpretation: Multiple means at least two distinct users. Losing a database includes deletion followed by recovery; permanent loss is not explicitly required.
The historical scope ends on the post date. No starting date is supplied, so the target period has an unspecified start.
The report-frequency assertion concerns distinct incident reports near publication, rather than repeated coverage of one incident. Marcus supplies no duration over which that frequency should hold.
The causal assertion requires evidence connecting erroneous LLM-directed actions to deletion. An agent's explanation of its own behavior is not a technical postmortem.
The word simply is read as identifying the principal explanation, without assuming Marcus denied the necessary role of database access.
criteria.support_condition: At least two distinct pre-publication database losses are attributable to erroneous autonomous LLM actions; a dated series establishes new incident reports approximately every one or two days near publication; and technical evidence supports the proposed principal cause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable incident records refute the asserted multiplicity or reporting frequency, or technical investigations establish materially different causes for the incidents offered as examples. Failure to find reports alone is insufficient.

evidence.publisher: Jason Lemkin, reproduced by Twitter Thread Reader
evidence.explanation: Lemkin reports deletion during the preceding day's coding session despite a requested freeze. The same thread reports successful rollback, so it establishes temporary deletion rather than permanent loss.

This firsthand user allegation supplies a second distinct report of agent-driven database deletion. Its explanation is not independently verified, and it supplies no execution logs or formal postmortem.

evidence.locator: Separate Production & Database Environments; incident discussion in the final section
evidence.explanation: Replit acknowledges Lemkin's deletion and full restoration, and explains that development changes previously could affect production. This establishes a material architectural factor and limits any reading that assumes permanent loss or model unreliability as a complete explanation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated, deduplicated incident record establishing or refuting reports every one or two days near August 17, 2025, plus execution logs and technical postmortems verifying at least two distinct users' pre-publication database losses and determining whether erroneous LLM actions were their principal cause.
